A channel row reads "clips, unread, 2 mentions"; a member row "Samira, admin, keeping the server warm". Never put a per-screen aria-label on a row instead. Web kit only so far.

docs.title: A keyboard list
docs.text:
A list the user moves through with the keyboard (a channel list, a member list, a picker) is built with useListFocus and the focus prop. The list is then one Tab stop: Up and Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the ends, typing a name jumps to it, and Enter or Space (or a click) chooses the row. Disabled rows are skipped.

const list = useListFocus({
  rows: channels.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, label: c.name, disabled: c.locked })), // every row, also unrendered ones
  selected: currentChannelId,           // the route: the pattern follows it, it never moves focus
  onSelect: (id) => markOpened(id),     // optional for links: the link has already navigated
});
<nav aria-label="Channels">
  <div {...list.listProps}>
    {channels.map((c) => (
      <ListRow key={c.id} primary={c.name} href={`/c/${c.id}`} selected={c.id === currentChannelId}
        disabled={c.locked} focus={list.rowFocus(c.id)} />
    ))}
  </div>
</nav>
  • Rows in a keyboard list are links or buttons; a plain row ignores focus. Keep disabled on the row and in rows the same.
  • focus is opaque: pass what rowFocus(id) returns, nothing else. The row's own onClick still runs; put an action in onClick or in onSelect, not in both.
  • Controls in trailing leave the Tab order while the row is in a keyboard list: Right moves from the row into them and Left back, and Up or Down go on to the next row. A row action that matters must also be reachable some other way (the row's menu, the opened page).
  • orientation: 'horizontal' adds Left and Right as movement (as Tabs does); wrap, selectionFollowsFocus and typeahead are the pattern's parameters.
  • A virtualised list passes the whole list as rows and a reveal(id) that scrolls the row into the rendered window; the host focuses it once it is there.

Stories: kit-list-focus--channel-list, kit-list-focus--channel-list-light, kit-list-focus--channel-list-focused, kit-list-focus--channel-list-focused-light, kit-list-focus--button-rows, kit-list-focus--selection-from-outside, kit-list-focus--selection-from-outside-light.

Stories: kit-list-row--states, kit-list-row--channels, kit-list-row--people, kit-list-row--long-names, kit-list-row--states-light, kit-list-row--states-tinted, kit-list-row--selected-with-trailing, kit-list-row--selected-with-trailing-light, kit-list-row--labelled, kit-list-row--labelled-light.

docs.title: PickerGrid
docs.text:
A grid of choices to pick one from: emoji, custom emoji, GIFs.

Use it when the reader picks one item out of many that are recognised by sight (the emoji picker, the GIF picker), usually in a Sheet with a search field in its top.

Do not use it when the items have names to read or a second line: use ListRow. For a few actions, use Buttons.

Sections of cells in rows that fill the width (as many columns as fit, each at least a control wide for glyph, so a cell stays a touch target on a phone). A section's title shows above it and names its group. The grid is one Tab stop (the last cell focused, else the first); the arrow keys move between cells in two dimensions and across sections, keeping the column; Home and End go to the first and last cell; Enter or Space picks. Every cell is a button named by its label. Pictures load lazily without a referrer. Each section is drawn only near the view (content-visibility: auto). With loadMore, the end of the grid coming into view (or focus reaching the last row) asks for more; footer shows under it (a spinner).

Prop Values Default Meaning label text none (required) Names the grid: "Emoji", "GIFs". sections id, title, items (id, label, glyph or src) none (required) The cells, by section. variant glyph, media glyph Square cells for emoji, or wide cells for GIF previews, cropped to fit. onPick function none (required) A cell was picked (its item and section id). loadMore function none Load more at the end. footer kit pieces none Under the last section. activeCellRef ref none The cell in the Tab order.

Stories: kit-picker-grid--grids, kit-picker-grid--grids-light, kit-picker-grid--grids-tinted, kit-picker-grid--narrow320; in the chat: channel-chat--emoji-picker, channel-chat--gif-picker.

docs.title: Table
docs.text:
Records laid out in rows, with one column for each kind of fact.

Use it when the user compares records by column: members and their roles, invites and their expiry dates.

Do not use it when you want to lay out a page. A table is for data only. Do not use it for a list of channels or people with an icon and a name each. Use ListRow.

The table has real table structure, so screen readers announce the columns. It has a thin line between rows, no stripes and no outer border. A cell takes text or kit components, such as a Pill or an IconButton. A table that is too wide for its space scrolls sideways inside its own box and not the page. The box can take keyboard focus, so a keyboard user can scroll it.

Prop Values Default Meaning label text none (required) Names the table for screen readers. It is not shown. columns a list of id, header and optionally align none (required) The columns. align is start or end; use end for numbers. rows a list of id and cells none (required) The records. cells holds one entry for each column id. empty text none Shown across the whole table when there are no rows.

Stories: kit-table--basic, kit-table--empty, kit-table--narrow, kit-table--basic-light, kit-table--basic-tinted.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
Children one under the other with a fixed space between them.

Use it when a few blocks inside an island, a Card or an overlay's body need the system's vertical rhythm: a heading, a field, then a list.

Do not use it when the rows are a list (ListRows sit flush, with no gap), or you need a whole screen arranged (use a layout template).

It is layout only: no surface, no padding, no semantics of its own.

Prop Values Default Meaning gap xs, sm, md, lg, xl none (required) The space between the children: 4, 8, 12, 16 or 24 pixels. children content none (required) The blocks. direction column, row column row puts the children side by side, centred on the cross axis, each keeping its own width (an Avatar, a button), except a Stack with fill. fill true, false false In a row: this Stack takes the room the others leave, and text in it can cut with an ellipsis (truncate). Use it for the name and line beside an avatar. It is for a child of a row only. align stretch, start stretch In a column: start keeps each child its own width (a Pill under a name), never wider than the Stack.

A row is for a few pieces that belong together on one line: an avatar, a name with its line under it, and a control at the end (a header, the user's card, a voice room's title). A list of things is still ListRows. A row centres its children on the cross axis; there is no justify or wrap.

direction, fill and align are web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

Stories: kit-stack--gaps, kit-stack--gaps-light, kit-stack--gaps-tinted, kit-stack--rows, kit-stack--rows-light, kit-stack--rows-tinted.

docs.title: CallStack
docs.text:
What the three-islands call slot holds while a call has video: the call's surface above the call bar.

Use it when you fill the callBar slot of Three islands with a call bar and something above it that can grow (the call's video, what it offers).

Do not use it when there is only the bar: put the bar in the slot as it is. Do not use it anywhere but the call slot.

The bar never gives up height: it is never shrunk, clipped or scrolled. The surface takes at most two fifths of the layout's height (the three-islands grid, a size container: what is left after the banner row, the on-screen keyboard and the safe areas, as 40cqh) and scrolls inside itself beyond that. When the frame is shorter still, the surface gives way further: the call slot gets only what the fixed rows and the pane's minimum leave, so the bar, its Leave and the screen's composer keep their room. While the on-screen keyboard is up the surface is left out and summary, one line, stands in for it. Layout only: no surface colour, no padding, no landmark.

Prop Values Default Meaning bar content none (required) The call bar. surface content none The call's video and what it offers, above the bar, bounded and scrolling. summary content none One line that stands in for surface while the keyboard is up. Without it nothing does.

Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

Stories: kit-call-stack--bounded, kit-call-stack--bounded-light, kit-call-stack--keyboard, kit-call-stack--bar-only.

docs.title: Chat pieces
docs.text: The pieces a conversation is built from: MessageRow, MessageText, ListSeparator, ReactionChip, Composer and JumpToLatest. They are web only so far; the native kit follows (issue #805). They hold no chat logic: the screen brings the data, the message list's scrolling and roving focus, drafts, mentions and sending.

docs.title: MessageRow
docs.text:
One message in a compact list (see Principles §4): the author's avatar, name and time on one line, the words under it, no bubble.

Use it when you show a message in a channel, a thread or a direct conversation.

Do not use it when you list people, channels or search results. Use ListRow. Do not wrap a message in a Card or a bubble.

A continued row is a follow-on from the same author: no avatar or name line, and the short time shows in the avatar's gutter on hover and while focus is in the row. Every row is still an article named by its author and time, so a screen reader hears who wrote a continued row. The name is a button when onOpenAuthor is given; the avatar is a pointer shortcut to the same place and is not a Tab stop. The row joins the list's roving focus through focus (the list owns which row is the one Tab stop). The actions open on a touch long press (500 ms, cancelled if the finger moves), a right-click, and Enter, the context-menu key or Shift+F10 on the row itself, through onOpenActions. Enter is how a keyboard that cannot hover (a tablet with a keyboard, which never shows the toolbar) reaches the actions; without onOpenActions the row leaves Enter alone. It is told how they were asked (touch, pointer or keyboard), so the screen can pick a Sheet or a Menu, and for a right-click or a long press where (x, y in the viewport), so a Menu can open at the cursor. A context menu that no pointer made (a screen reader's "show menu", the Menu key) is a keyboard request with no point: anchor the Menu to the row and return focus to it.

Tab inside a row. A message list is one Tab stop: the row that holds the list's roving focus (focus.tabStop). The controls inside a row (links, mentions, reactions, a quote, attachments, Retry and Delete, a footer button, the name) are Tab stops only in that row and in a row focus is already in; in every other row they are tabIndex -1, still pressable and still found by a screen reader's own navigation. So Tab from the focused row walks its own controls and then leaves the list. A row without focus keeps every control a Tab stop. Kit controls follow this by themselves; a control you put in a slot that is not a kit piece must read useRowTabIndex too. The row carries data-row-focus-target, which the list core's roving focus moves to.

A long press does not start on a link, button or field inside the row: those keep their own press (a long press on a link is the browser's "copy link"). The click that follows a long press is swallowed, so a reaction under the finger is not toggled. While a finger is held down the row turns off the iOS callout and text selection; with a mouse, message text stays selectable. A field inside the row (an inline editor) keeps its own context menu.

actions is a toolbar at the row's top end that shows on hover and while focus is in the row; Tab from the row reaches its buttons. Hidden, it is not there at all (visibility: hidden): Tab does not walk the hidden toolbars of other rows and a tap cannot hit one. While a Menu or Popover opened from it is open (its button is aria-expanded), the toolbar stays, so closing it returns focus to that button. On a device that cannot hover it is never shown: the actions come from the long press and the context-menu key. Events from a Menu or picker opened from a slot are not the row's: they reach the row through React's tree, from outside its DOM, and are ignored.

A failed row says why with failedReason ("Timed out until 8:40 PM"), or "Not sent". While retrying, Retry is busy (it keeps focus and ignores presses), so a double tap cannot send twice.

To edit a message in place, the body is a Composer with inline and mode="save": it draws no outer padding and does not move the toasts.

Prop Values Default Meaning author text none (required) Who wrote it. avatarSrc, avatarColour image, #rrggbb none The author's picture and colour. time text none (required) The short time shown. dateTime ISO 8601 none The machine time of <time>. timeLabel text none The full date and time: read, and shown as the time's tooltip. continued true, false false A follow-on from the same author. mentioned true, false false It mentions the reader: an accent rail and tint. highlighted true, false false The jump target: a stronger accent tint while set. state sent, pending, failed sent Pending is dimmed and busy, "Sending…". Failed says "Not sent". failedReason text none Why it failed, shown in place of "Not sent". retrying true, false false A retry is on its way: Retry is busy and ignores presses. edited, pinned true, false false "(edited)" and the pin mark after the time. quote, body, attachments, reactions, footer kit pieces none The slots, in that order. Reactions wrap. body is a MessageText, or an inline Composer to edit. actions IconButtons none The hover and focus toolbar (compact and wide; never on a device that cannot hover). onOpenActions function of { via, x, y } (touch, pointer) or { via } (keyboard) none Long press, right-click or the context-menu key, and where. onOpenAuthor function none The name and avatar open the profile. onRetry, onDelete function none Retry and Delete on a failed row. focus tabStop, onKeyDown, onFocus none The list's roving focus.

Stories: kit-message-row--states, kit-message-row--states-light, kit-message-row--states-tinted, kit-message-row--long-content, kit-message-row--long-content-light, kit-message-row--actions, kit-message-row--actions-light, kit-message-row--editing, kit-message-row--editing-light, kit-message-row--toolbar-tab-order.

docs.title: MessageText
docs.text:
A message's words, drawn from segments the chat data layer has already parsed.

Use it when you show the body of a message, a quote or a search result.

Do not use it when you show text you wrote for the interface. Use Text.

The segment kinds are text (with bold, italic, strike), code, codeBlock, link (with the same bold, italic, strike, so a link in a bold span stays bold), mention (user, role, channel, everyone; me when it is of the reader, unavailable when the reader cannot open it) and emoji (a community's custom emoji, :name: when it has no image). It is dir="auto", keeps line breaks, and wraps an unbroken run instead of overflowing. Italic is Figtree's own italic face.

Only http and https links are links; any other address is drawn as text. A link always shows its own address: there are no masked links, so a label cannot point somewhere else. What is shown is the parsed address as the parser writes it, never decoded: a lookalike host reads as punycode (xn--pple-43d.com, not аpple.com), and a space, an invisible character or a bidi control in the path stays %xx. An address with a user name or password (https://bank.example@evil.example/) is drawn as text, not a link.

A user mention is a button when onMention is given; a channel mention with an href is a link whose plain click calls onMention. Only an app-internal href is followed: a hash route (#/c/clips) or a path with one leading slash (/c/clips), with no // and no . or .. segment in the path. Anything else (//host, /.//host, data:, https:) draws the mention as text that is not a link. A mention of the reader adds ", mentions you" to its name. Code uses the platform's monospace font. Emoji-only messages are drawn at text size, as in the classic chat.

Prop Values Default Meaning segments a list of segments none (required) The words. onMention function of the mention none A mention was pressed.

Stories: kit-message-text--segments, kit-message-text--segments-light, kit-message-text--segments-tinted.

docs.title: ListSeparator
docs.text:
A break in a list of messages.

Use it when a new day starts (day: "Today") or the unread messages start (unread: "New").

Do not use it when you head a group in a list of channels or people. Use a section heading.

It is a separator named by its label. A long label is cut with an ellipsis.

Prop Values Default Meaning variant day, unread none (required) A centred day tag, or an accent line with its tag at the end. label text none (required) The tag, and the separator's name.

Stories: kit-list-separator--variants, kit-list-separator--variants-light, kit-list-separator--variants-tinted.

docs.title: ReactionChip
docs.text:
One reaction under a message: the emoji and how many reacted with it.

Use it when you show a reaction the reader can add or take back.

Do not use it when you show a status or a role. Use Pill. The quick reactions and the picker are the screen's.

A toggle button, pressed when it is the reader's (an accent ring and tint, so not by colour alone). Its name is "Laugh reaction, 4". Counts up to 999 are drawn in full, above that in a compact form ("1.3K"); the name keeps the exact count. Pill was not made a toggle: it is a static tag and has no pressed state.

Prop Values Default Meaning emoji text none (required) The emoji, or a custom emoji's :name: as its fallback. src image none A custom emoji's image. label text none (required) What it is, in words, for its name. count number none (required) How many reacted. mine true, false false The reader reacted with it. onToggle function none (required) Adds or removes the reader's reaction. aria-disabled true, false false The reader may not react: focusable, named, a press does not toggle. onUnavailablePress function none An unavailable chip was pressed: say why (useAnnounce). onShowPeople function none Shows who reacted (the screen's list): a touch long press, a right-click, or the context-menu key or Shift+F10 on the chip. A plain press still toggles; the row's actions do not open. Works on an unavailable or busy chip. busy true, false false The toggle is on its way: aria-busy and aria-disabled, presses ignored.

Stories: kit-reaction-chip--states, kit-reaction-chip--states-light, kit-reaction-chip--states-tinted.

docs.title: Composer
docs.text:
The chrome of a message composer.

Use it when the reader writes a message, a reply or an edit.

Do not use it when you need a form field. Use TextField.

A field that grows to a cap and then scrolls (keyboard 2 lines, phone 4, desktop 10), a leading attach button, a trailing emoji slot and Send. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a line (off on touch with submitOnEnter); text being composed with an input method never sends, including the Enter that picks a candidate in Safari (isComposing or keyCode 229). While an input method composes no key reaches the screen's onKeyDown either (Escape closes the candidate list, it never cancels a reply or an edit). Otherwise the screen's onKeyDown runs first and can take a key with preventDefault. Send is never disabled: with nothing to send it reads as unavailable (onSendUnavailablePress can say why), and while sending it is busy, while the field stays editable. An unavailable attach button is focusable and aria-disabled, and onAttachUnavailablePress says why. A banner strip says it is a reply or an edit and has a cancel button. A notice takes the place of the field when the reader cannot write. It keeps toasts clear of itself.

mode="save" is for editing a message: the button is "Save changes" with a check. inline draws it inside a message row (the row's body): no outer padding, and it does not keep toasts clear of itself, so an editor mid-list or scrolled out of view does not move the toasts. Inline in save mode there is no Save button: a small line under the field says "escape to cancel • enter to save" (Discord's), and its words "cancel" and "save" are text buttons ("Cancel editing", "Save changes"); without submitOnEnter (touch) it reads "Cancel • Save". onCancel is its cancel.

onPasteFiles gets the files among what was pasted into the field (a picture, a copied file); plain text pastes as usual. dropTarget draws the composer as where dragged files go (a dashed accent outline over it with the label); the drag events belong to the conversation (ChatPane's dropZone).

Prop Values Default Meaning label text none (required) The field's name and placeholder: "Message #general". placeholder text label A different placeholder. value, onChange text, function none (required) The draft. onSubmit function none (required) Send, or save. mode send, save send "Send message" with the Send icon, or "Save changes" with a check. inline true, false false Inside a message row: no padding, no toast clearance. canSend true, false text not blank Whether there is something to send. onSendUnavailablePress function none Send was pressed with nothing to send: say why. sending true, false false Send is busy. submitOnEnter true, false true Enter sends. onKeyDown function none The screen's keys, first. onCaretMove function none The caret or selection moved (typing, keys, a tap): a suggestion list follows it. cap keyboard, phone, desktop desktop How far the field grows. onAttach function none Shows the attach button. attachUnavailable true, false false The attach button is aria-disabled and does not call onAttach. onAttachUnavailablePress function none The unavailable attach button was pressed: say why. emoji IconButtons none The emoji (and GIF) buttons. onCancel function none Inline save mode: the hint's "cancel". onPasteFiles function none Files pasted into the field. dropTarget active, label none Files are dragged over the conversation: the drop look. banner kind (reply, editing), title, detail, cancelLabel, onCancel none The reply or editing strip. notice text, icon none Replaces the field. attachments kit pieces none The tray of queued files. popup listId, activeId none A suggestion list is open: the field is its combobox input. suggestions a SuggestionList none The open list, drawn over the conversation just above the composer, across its width. Not under a notice.

Stories: kit-composer--states, kit-composer--states-light, kit-composer--states-tinted, kit-composer--at-cap, kit-composer--at-phone-cap, kit-composer--at-keyboard-cap, kit-composer--mention-list, kit-composer--mention-list-light, kit-composer--mention-list-tinted, kit-composer--mention-list-loading; inline editing in a row: kit-message-row--editing.

Inside a MessageRow (inline editing) the field owns its keys: ↑, ↓, Home, End and Escape move its caret or cancel the edit and never reach the list's roving focus.

docs.title: JumpToLatest
docs.text:
The floating control that takes the reader back to the newest message.

Use it when the reader has scrolled away from the bottom of a message list.

Do not use it when you need a button in the page. Use Button.

It places itself centred, lg above the bottom edge of its positioned container (the list region), over the rows. With newCount it reads "3 new" in the accent (above 99, "99+ new"); its name is "Jump to latest, 3 new messages".

Prop Values Default Meaning onJump function none (required) Go to the newest message. newCount number none Messages that arrived while away. busy true, false false Loading the latest: aria-busy and aria-disabled, presses ignored.

Stories: kit-jump-to-latest--states, kit-jump-to-latest--states-light, kit-jump-to-latest--states-tinted.

docs.title: ChatPane
docs.text:
A conversation inside the centre island: its header at the top, the message list filling what is left, and the composer under it. The list region is the positioned container the floating parts place themselves in: the typing line at its bottom (over the room the list core keeps under its last row) and JumpToLatest. It also holds the polite live region that says new messages the reader cannot see. A screen never positions these itself.

Use it when you build a channel, DM or thread conversation. Do not use it for a list that is not messages.

Prop Values Default Meaning header kit pieces none The conversation's header (Back, its name, buttons). list a message list none The list. Only it scrolls. state kit pieces none In the list's place, centred: skeleton rows, empty, no access, an error with Try again. typing a TypingLine none Floats at the bottom of the list region. jump a JumpToLatest none Floats over the bottom of the list region. announcement text none Said politely, never shown ("2 new messages from aiko"). composer a Composer none Under the list. cover a ChatPane none A second conversation over this one, filling the pane (a thread over its channel). This one stays mounted underneath (its scroll and draft kept) but hidden and inert, and says nothing, until the cover goes. dropZone onDragEnter, onDragOver, onDragLeave, onDrop none Files dropped anywhere on the conversation (the shared drop zone's handlers); not while covered.

Stories: kit-chat-pane--conversation, kit-chat-pane--conversation-light, kit-chat-pane--conversation-tinted, kit-chat-pane--with-composer, kit-chat-pane--covered, kit-chat-pane--covered-light, kit-chat-pane--long-history (2,000 rows on the list core: the performance check).

docs.title: MessageQuote
docs.text:
The message a reply answers, above the reply's words (MessageRow's quote): the author and one line that gives way with an ellipsis. With onOpen it is a button named "Reply to aiko: …" that shows the original (a jump in the list). A deleted original reads "Original message was deleted" and opens nothing.

Prop Values Default Meaning author text none (required) Who wrote the original. line text none (required) One line of it. deleted true, false false The original is gone. onOpen function none Shows the original.

Stories: kit-message-quote--states, kit-message-quote--states-light, kit-message-quote--states-tinted.

docs.title: AttachmentTile
docs.text:
A file sent with a message (MessageRow's attachments). An image is drawn in a box sized from its known width and height, shrunk to fit 320 by 240 (240 by 160 when the size is unknown), so a picture that arrives late never moves the list; the picture loads lazily and pressing it opens the image (the screen's MediaViewer). A video gets the same box with its still (poster) and Play ("Play video clip.mp4, 12 MB"); an audio file is a row with Play ("Play audio voice-note.ogg, 420 KB"). Nothing plays, and nothing is fetched, until it is pressed: onOpen asks the screen for the address, and once the screen gives it as src the tile becomes the browser's own player in the same place and starts; when Play had focus, focus moves to the player. Any other file is a row with its name and size; pressing it downloads the file. While busy presses are ignored (the control stays focusable). A picture from another site (a GIF someone linked) is remote: it loads without a Referer, though the site still sees the reader's address.

A file on its way uses the same tile. Queued in the composer's tray it has no onOpen (nothing to press: a group named "notes.txt, 2 KB"), a thumbnail in the paperclip's place when it is a picture (src on a file), and a Remove button (onRemove, "Remove notes.txt"). Uploading under a pending message it has a bar (progress, "Uploading notes.txt") and, when the upload failed, the reason in the danger tone with Retry (error, onRetry, "Retry uploading notes.txt").

Prop Values Default Meaning kind image, video, audio, file none (required) A picture, a video, an audio file, or a file row. name text none (required) The file's name. detail text none Its size, written for people ("2.4 MB"). src image or media address none The picture (a preview); a quiet fill until it is known. On a video or audio, the address to play: given, the tile is the player. poster image none A video's still, under Play. remote true, false false The picture comes from another site: no Referer. onLoadError function none The picture could not be drawn: the screen may draw something else (a GIF falls back to its link). width, height pixels none The image's own size: the box is sized from them. onOpen function none Opens the image or downloads the file. Without it the tile is not pressable (a queued file). busy true, false false The open or download is on its way. onRemove function none A Remove button beside the tile. progress 0 to 100 none An upload bar under the tile. error text none The upload failed: shown in place of detail, in the danger tone. onRetry function none With error: Retry.

Stories: kit-attachment-tile--states, kit-attachment-tile--states-light, kit-attachment-tile--states-tinted, kit-attachment-tile--queued, kit-attachment-tile--queued-light, kit-attachment-tile--media-states, kit-attachment-tile--media-states-light.

docs.title: LinkCard
docs.text:
A link's preview under a message (MessageRow's attachments): the site with its icon, the page's title and summary (two lines each at most), and its picture.

Use it when the server has a preview of a link in a message.

Do not use it when you show a file (AttachmentTile) or a reply's original (MessageQuote). Do not use Card for it: Card is a surface for controls, not one link with a picture.

The whole card is one link that opens in a new tab ("The ridge loop, Trailheads, opens in a new tab"), with no opener and no Referer. Only an http or https address without a user name is a link (the same check as MessageText); anything else is drawn as a plain group. The picture sits in a box of fixed shape (1.91:1, the shape preview pictures are made for), so it never changes the card's height when it arrives; one that fails leaves the box empty. Both pictures come from other sites: they load without a Referer, the banner lazily, and only an address that passes the same check as the link is drawn. A card that arrives after the message (the server fetches previews later) grows its row; the message list follows the growth when the reader is at the bottom.

Prop Values Default Meaning href address none (required) The page. site text none (required) The site's name or host, with the author when known. title text none The page's title. description text none The page's summary. imageSrc image address none The page's picture. iconSrc image address none The site's icon; the link icon without it.

Stories: kit-link-card--states, kit-link-card--states-light, kit-link-card--states-tinted.

docs.title: TypingLine
docs.text:
Who is typing, one quiet line at the bottom of the message list (ChatPane's typing): "aiko is typing…", "aiko and dropbear are typing…", "aiko and 3 others are typing…". It is 32 px tall, the room the list core keeps under its last row, so it never covers a message. A long name gives way; nothing is drawn while nobody types.

Prop Values Default Meaning names list of names none (required) Who is typing, first to start first.

Stories: kit-typing-line--states, kit-typing-line--states-light, kit-typing-line--states-tinted.

docs.title: SuggestionList
docs.text:
The suggestions a composer offers while the reader types a mention (Composer's suggestions, with popup): a listbox the field drives as a combobox. Focus never leaves the field: ↑ and ↓ move the highlight (read through the field's aria-activedescendant), Enter or Tab picks and Escape closes, all in the screen's keys. A press on an option picks it without taking focus from the field, so the on-screen keyboard stays up. A person shows their avatar, anything else (@here, a mention group) an icon; a long name gives way. About six rows show, then it scrolls. Web only so far (native follows, #805).

Use it when a field offers completions as the reader types. Do not use it for a list of actions (use Menu) or a choice in a form (use SelectField).

Prop Values Default Meaning id text none (required) The listbox's id: the composer's popup.listId. label text none (required) Names the list: "Mention suggestions". options key, label, detail, avatar or icon none (required) The suggestions. activeIndex number none (required) The highlighted option, or -1. optionId function none (required) Each option's element id (the composer's popup.activeId). onPick function none (required) An option was pressed. loading true, false false Nothing to show yet: a "Loading…" row, aria-busy.

Stories: kit-composer--mention-list, kit-composer--mention-list-light, kit-composer--mention-list-tinted, kit-composer--mention-list-loading.

docs.title: Which overlay
docs.text:
Six components float above the page. Choose by what the thing holds and by how much it should stop the user. For a message about something that happened, use Toast or Alert instead.

Overlay What it holds Blocks the rest of the page? How it closes Tooltip A few words of text No It closes on its own when the pointer or focus leaves, or on Escape. Menu A list of actions on one thing Yes, until it closes Choosing an item, Escape, a press outside, or Tab. Popover A small piece of interface: a short form, a picker, a few controls No Escape or a press outside. Dialog A decision that needs an answer Yes A button in it, Escape, or a press on the dimmed page. Sheet Browsing many things, or a longer task Yes Its Close button, a button in it, Escape, or a press on the dimmed page. MediaViewer Pictures, one at a time, filling the screen Yes Its Close button, Escape, or a press beside the picture.

Overlays stack in the order they were opened, and a tooltip sits above all of them. A Menu, a select list or a Popover that opens from inside a Dialog is on top of the Dialog, and Escape closes the innermost layer first. A layer opened from inside another closes with it: when the Dialog closes, the Popover open in it closes too, and its onClose is called. Nothing in a screen sets a layer number, and no screen handles Escape or a press outside for an overlay: the overlay stack does (see Overlay stack).

Inside a Dialog, a Popover, Tooltip, Menu or select list is drawn within the Dialog, so its focus trap lets focus into them. The other way round, a Dialog opened from a Popover works too (and the Popover stays open under it).

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
A short list of actions that opens from a control, such as a "More" button.

Use it when the user picks one action to do to a thing: rename, copy a link, delete.

Do not use it when the user picks a value for a field (use SelectField), or when the panel needs controls other than actions (use Popover). A Menu closes after one choice.

The menu opens from an anchor, which is the element that opened it. Each item has a label and does one thing when chosen. An item may have an icon, keyboard shortcut keys shown as KeyCaps, a danger tone for a destructive action, and a disabled state. A divider groups items. Put the destructive item last, apart from the rest.

Prop Values Default Meaning open true, false none (required) Whether the menu is showing. anchor the element it opens from none (required) Where the menu sits. onClose a function none (required) Called when the menu should close. label text none (required) Names the menu for screen readers. items a list of entries none (required) Each entry is an item or a divider. See below. placement bottom-start, bottom-end, top-start, top-end bottom-start Which side of the anchor, and which edge it lines up with.

An item has an id, a label and an onSelect function, and optionally an icon, a shortcut (a list of keys, one KeyCap each), a tone (default or danger) and disabled. A divider is an entry with an id and divider set to true.

Stories: kit-menu--open, kit-menu--placements, kit-menu--open-light, kit-menu--open-tinted.

docs.title: Popover
docs.text:
A small floating panel tied to a control. It holds a little interface of its own.

Use it when the user needs a few controls close to the thing they act on: an emoji picker, a short form, a set of filters.

Do not use it when the content is a list of actions (use Menu), a few words of explanation (use Tooltip), or a decision the user must answer before going on (use Dialog). A Popover may open from a control inside a Dialog: it is drawn within the Dialog and takes focus there.

A Popover does not block the page. It has no dimmed backdrop, and the page behind it can still scroll. It is opened from an anchor, the element that opened it. It must always have a label, which names the panel for screen readers. The panel flips to the other side of the anchor when there is no room.

Prop Values Default Meaning open true, false none (required) Whether the popover is showing. anchor the element it opens from none (required) Where the popover sits. Focus returns to it on close. onClose a function none (required) Called on Escape and on a press outside. label text none (required) Names the panel for screen readers. placement bottom-start, bottom-end, top-start, top-end bottom-start Which side of the anchor, and which edge it lines up with. padding none, md, lg md The space inside the panel. Use none when the content brings its own, such as a list of rows.

Other overlays can open from inside a Popover: a select list, a Menu or a Dialog. A press or an Escape in them belongs to them. The Popover closes only when the press or the key is outside all of them. A tall Popover has no maximum height; keep its content short.

Stories: kit-popover--open, kit-popover--open-compact, kit-popover--open-light, kit-popover--inside-dialog.

docs.title: Tooltip
docs.text:
A few words of text that name or explain a control.

Use it when a control shows only an icon and a short name helps, or when a control needs one line of explanation.

Do not use it when the text is long, holds a link or a button, or is the only place a piece of information lives. A Tooltip holds text only. Make it a few words. People on touch screens never see tooltips. So a tooltip repeats or explains what the control is called. It never carries something the user must know. Put that on the page, or in a Popover.

A Tooltip wraps one control. The control keeps its own name for screen readers. The tooltip adds its text as a description while it is showing. It is added to the element that takes focus (the input of a field, the button of a Switch) and sits beside any description the control already has, such as helper text.

A tooltip on a disabled control will not show: a disabled control takes no focus, and some browsers send it no pointer events. Put that text beside the control instead. The panel cannot be hovered, so it closes as soon as the pointer leaves the control. That is fine for a few words; it is one more reason not to put more in it. A tap on a text field never opens it.

Prop Values Default Meaning label text none (required) The text. Never anything clickable. placement top, bottom, left, right top Which side of the control. It moves to the other side when there is no room.

Stories: kit-tooltip--shown, kit-tooltip--long-label, kit-tooltip--shown-light.

docs.title: Dialog
docs.text:
A box that interrupts the screen to ask for a decision.

Use it when the user must answer before going on: confirm a deletion, give a name, accept a choice. It is the modal for a decision. It dims the page and nothing behind it can be used until it closes.

Do not use it when the information can sit on the page (use Alert), when it is a passing notice (use Toast), or when the user can carry on without answering (use Popover).

Rules for the actions:

  • Put the safe action first, such as "Cancel". Focus starts on the first action, so a stray Enter does the safe thing. On a phone the buttons stack in the same order, with the safe action on top.
  • A destructive confirmation names what will be lost, in its title or its description: "Delete #general?", "This removes 214 messages for everyone." A bare "Are you sure?" is not enough.
  • Use a Button with the danger variant for the destructive action.

The parent decides whether the dialog closes. onClose is called on Escape and on a press on the dimmed page, and the dialog stays open until open is false. onClose says why: 'escape' or 'scrim', which the parent may refuse (unsaved changes), or 'parentClosed'. A dialog opened from inside another layer (a Popover, say) closes when that layer closes; then onClose('parentClosed') is a notice, not a request: the dialog is already closed whatever open says, so set open to false, even when there are unsaved changes.

A select list, a Menu, a Popover or a Tooltip may open from inside a Dialog. Escape closes that layer first and the Dialog on the next press. The dialog has the role dialog, not alertdialog, so a scrim press closes a destructive confirmation too; keep the safe action first.

Prop Values Default Meaning open true, false none (required) Whether the dialog is showing. onClose a function, given 'escape', 'scrim' or 'parentClosed' none (required) Called on Escape, on a press on the dimmed page, and when the layer it was opened from closes. title text none (required) Names the dialog. It is the heading. description text none A line under the title that says more. children content none The body, such as a field. It sits between the description and the actions. actions Buttons none (required) The buttons, safe action first. size sm, md sm The width. sm is 400 pixels and md is 560. On a narrow screen the dialog keeps the page gutter on both sides.

Stories: kit-dialog--confirm, kit-dialog--with-content, kit-dialog--phone, kit-dialog--confirm-light, kit-dialog--confirm-tinted, kit-dialog--with-select, kit-dialog--from-card.

docs.title: ConfirmDialog
docs.text:
The dialog that asks before something cannot be undone, runs the action, and stays open with the error if it fails.

Use it when the user asks for an irreversible action (delete a channel, leave a community). Get it from useConfirmDestructive, which owns the phases (see Behaviour); the hook's dialog is this component.

Do not use it when the action can be undone (offer Undo in a Toast), or when the dialog asks for more than a yes (use Dialog).

Prop Values Default Meaning phase idle, confirming, working, failed none (required) idle is closed. error text or null none (required) The failure shown while phase is failed. title text none (required) Names what is lost: "Delete #general?". description text none (required) What goes with it: "This removes 214 messages for everyone." confirmLabel text none (required) The danger button, and the retry button after a failure: "Delete channel". onConfirm a function none (required) The confirm button. onCancel a function, given 'button', 'escape' or 'scrim' none (required) Cancel, Escape or a press on the dimmed page. onPresence a function, given true or false none (required) false: the dialog went away without an answer (the layer it was opened from closed, or it left the page). true: it is on the page again.
  • Cancel comes first and takes focus; the danger button is second.
  • While working, the danger button is busy (it keeps focus and its name) and Cancel is aria-disabled: unavailable, but still focusable, so focus that sits on it does not fall to the page. Escape and a press on the dimmed page do nothing.
  • After a failure the error shows as a danger Alert in the body, Cancel works again, and the same button retries.
  • Rendered inside a Popover, Sheet or other layer that can close while the action works, a failure after that close shows only as a danger toast: the screen must render the toast region (AppFrame always does; a story or test outside it renders <ToastRegion />).
  • Words: Writing.

Stories: kit-confirm-dialog--confirming, kit-confirm-dialog--confirming-light, kit-confirm-dialog--working, kit-confirm-dialog--working-light, kit-confirm-dialog--failed, kit-confirm-dialog--failed-light, kit-confirm-dialog--timed-out, kit-confirm-dialog--failed-long-text, kit-confirm-dialog--from-menu, kit-confirm-dialog--from-menu-never-ends, kit-confirm-dialog--parent-closes-then-fails.

docs.title: MediaViewer
docs.text:
A message's pictures, one at a time, filling the screen.

Use it when the reader opens a picture from a message to see it full size.

Do not use it when you ask a question (Dialog) or show a list (Sheet). It is not a gallery of a whole channel.

The name of the picture is the heading, with "2 of 5" beside it when there are several, and Download (when the screen gives onDownload) and Close at the top. The picture is as large as fits, never enlarged past the screen. Previous and Next sit at its sides when there are several; at either end the button stays, unavailable, so focus on it is never dropped. ← and → step too (reversed in a right-to-left page), and so does a sideways swipe; pinch zoom stays the browser's. Until the picture is known a spinner shows ("Loading sunset.png"); one that fails says "Couldn't load the picture". It is a modal layer like Dialog: the page behind is inert, focus starts on Close and is held inside, Escape, Close and a press beside the picture call onClose ('escape', 'button', 'scrim'), and focus returns to what opened it. The background is the ground colour of the palette, in light and dark.

Prop Values Default Meaning open true, false none (required) Whether it shows. onClose function, given 'escape', 'scrim', 'button' or 'parentClosed' none (required) Asked to close. items list of { src?, name, alt?, failed? } none (required) The pictures, in order. index number none (required) The one showing. onIndexChange function none (required) Another one was asked for. onDownload function none A Download button for the one showing. downloading true, false false The download is on its way.

Stories: kit-media-viewer--single, kit-media-viewer--single-light, kit-media-viewer--several, kit-media-viewer--several-light, kit-media-viewer--several-tinted, kit-media-viewer--tall, kit-media-viewer--loading, kit-media-viewer--long-name, kit-media-viewer--failed.

Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

docs.title: Island
docs.text:
The large surface of the app: a rounded panel that floats on the ground and holds a part of the screen.

Use it when you group a part of a screen: a list of channels, the messages, a member list. Every part of a screen sits on an island.

Do not use it when you want a block inside an island. Use Card. Do not put an island inside an island.

An island has no border and is lifted by a shadow. It does not set the gap to the next island. The layout does. In a row of islands, give each one its width from the layout, because an island is only as wide as its content.

docs.title: Which label and element
docs.text:
An island is a page region only when it has a label. Give it one when the part is something people jump to, and then pick the element with as:

  • nav: places to go, such as the list of channels. It must have a label: several unnamed navigation landmarks cannot be told apart.
  • aside: supporting content beside the main content, such as a member list. It must have a label.
  • main: the main content of the page. Use it once per page.
  • section: any other named part. This is the default. Without a label it is only a box, not a region.
  • div: a plain box, with no meaning for screen readers. It cannot have a label, because a name on a box with no role is not allowed.
Prop Values Default Meaning children content none (required) What the island holds. as section, aside, nav, main, div section The page element. See above. label text none Names the region for screen readers. Required for nav and aside, not allowed for div. padding none, md, lg lg The space inside. Use none when the content brings its own, such as a list of rows. scroll true, false false The island fills the height its parent gives it, and its content scrolls inside it, never the page. footer content none A block that stays at the island's foot while the content above it scrolls (the user's own card in the left island). It sits inside the island's padding, a small gap below the content. Pass null while there is nothing to show: the island keeps its structure, so its content is never rebuilt. A footer taller than the island is cut off (the body shrinks to nothing first), and it adds no safe-area inset of its own. Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system). id text none The id of the element.

Without scroll, whatever is wider or taller than the island is cut off. With scroll, the parent must give the island a height. An island is the surface layer for everything inside it.

Stories: kit-island--layout, kit-island--scrolling, kit-island--with-footer, kit-island--with-footer-light, kit-island--with-footer-tinted, kit-island--paddings, kit-island--layout-light, kit-island--layout-tinted.

docs.title: Card
docs.text:
A soft-filled block inside an island. It is plain, or it is one button or one link that covers the whole card.

Use it when you show a self-contained thing in an island with its own content: a voice room with the people in it, a block of settings.

Do not use it when the thing is one row in a list. Use ListRow. Do not put a Card on the ground, or inside another Card.

A card that is a button or a link is one control, named by its text. If the text is not enough, give it a label. Because the whole card is the control, a clickable Card holds no other controls: a button inside a button is invalid and its clicks would reach the card. Types cannot see inside children, so in development the Card logs one error that names it when it finds a button, link, input, select, textarea or element with a tabindex inside it. Use a plain Card with the controls inside, or a ListRow with a trailing control. A plain card may hold any kit components.

Kit pieces adapt on their own when they sit on a Card, which is the fill layer. A soft Button, a neutral Pill, a field, a segmented Tabs track, a KeyCap, a Skeleton, an Alert, an AvatarStack "+N", the initials of an Avatar and the rail of a Slider or LinearProgress draw on the surface colour instead of the fill, so they stay visible; hover tints on ghost and text buttons, tabs, checks and rows are mixed over the Card's fill. A Card inside a Card is surface, not fill on fill (but avoid it: see above). A Dialog, Sheet, Menu or Popover opened from inside a Card is its own surface layer and draws normally. You do not do anything for this.

docs.title: Two signs for "this one"
docs.text:
The Card and the ListRow each have a sign for the current thing, and they mean different things. Never swap them.

Sign Where What it means Accent outline selected on a Card You are in this (a voice room you joined), or this is the current item. Solid accent pill selected on a ListRow The selected row in a list, such as the channel you are in.

The outline is drawn as a border that is always there and is clear when the card is not selected, so selecting never changes the size of the card. A selected card is announced as current.

Prop Values Default Meaning children content none (required) What the card holds. selected true, false false The accent outline. padding md, lg md The space inside. onClick a function none Makes the card a button. href an address none Makes the card a link. Do not pass both onClick and href. label text none The accessible name of a button or link card, when its text is not enough. id text none The id of the element.

Stories: kit-card--voice-rooms, kit-card--clickable, kit-card--paddings, kit-card--nested, kit-card--nested-light, kit-card--voice-rooms-light, kit-card--voice-rooms-tinted.

docs.title: Dock
docs.text:
The bar where the user moves between communities and goes to the inbox. It is a pill-shaped bar of DockItems, icon buttons and dividers.

Use it when you build the community switcher of a screen.

Do not use it when you need tabs for views of a page (use Tabs) or a list of places with names (use ListRow in an island).

A Dock must have a label. It names the navigation for screen readers.

Prop Values Default Meaning label text none (required) Names the navigation. children DockItems, IconButtons and DockDividers none (required) What is on the bar. bottomBar true, false false The bar is the bottom edge of a phone screen. It adds the home-indicator inset (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) as a bottom margin, so it does not sit under the indicator. Leave it off when the bar is mid-layout. start IconButtons and DockDividers none Items fixed at the start of the bar, such as the Inbox: they never scroll out of sight. end IconButtons and DockDividers none Items fixed at the end of the bar, such as "All communities": they never scroll out of sight.

Only the children scroll, between start and end. The scrolling region keeps space.sm inside each edge, so a count or a dot at the edge item is never cut off, and an edge with more beyond it fades out (space.xl wide), which says there is more to scroll to. Use start and end for the items a user must always reach (the inbox, "All communities") whenever the communities may not fit. Web kit only so far for start, end, the inset and the fade.

Put an IconButton on the bar for a thing that is not a community, such as the inbox. Use a DockDivider between groups: it is a thin vertical line, and it has no options and is hidden from screen readers. A bar that holds more than fits scrolls sideways, and keeps the current item in view, again when the bar changes size (a rotation). See "What the browser does for us". Its items draw on the surface layer. Where the bar sits on screen, and keeping page content clear of it, belong to the app shell.

A keyboard Dock. With many communities the bar is one list, not one Tab stop per item. Build it like a keyboard list, with orientation: 'horizontal': pass useListFocus(...).bar as the Dock's focus, and rowFocus(id) as the focus of every DockItem and IconButton on the bar. Tab then enters on the selected (current) item, Left, Right, Home and End move along the bar, typing a name jumps to it, and the next Tab leaves the bar. The focused item scrolls into view inside the bar, never the page. The bar itself is then tabindex="-1", because Firefox would otherwise make a scrolling bar a Tab stop of its own. The same on a phone's bottom bar (bottomBar).

// rows: every item on the bar, in the order they are drawn: Inbox, each community, All.
// Each id is the id the item gets from rowFocus(id); label is what typeahead matches.
const rows = [
  { id: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', disabled: false },
  ...communities.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, label: c.name, disabled: false })),
  { id: 'all', label: 'All communities', disabled: false },
];
const list = useListFocus({
  rows,
  selected: currentId,                  // the current community's id, or null
  orientation: 'horizontal',
  onSelect: (id) => id === 'all' && openAllSheet(),   // see below
});
<Dock
  label="Communities"
  focus={list.bar}
  start={<IconButton icon="Inbox" label="Inbox" badge={9} focus={list.rowFocus('inbox')} />}
  end={<IconButton icon="LayoutGrid" label="All communities" focus={list.rowFocus('all')} />}
>
  {communities.map((c) => (
    <DockItem key={c.id} name={c.name} href={`#/community/${c.id}`} current={c.id === currentId}
      unread={c.mentions} unreadLabel="mentions" focus={list.rowFocus(c.id)} />
  ))}
</Dock>
  • rows must hold the Inbox and All items as well as the communities. An item whose id is not in rows gets tabindex="-1" and is skipped by every key: it cannot be reached with the keyboard.
  • A disabled IconButton ignores focus, so its row must say disabled: true as well, or an arrow lands on a button that cannot take focus and the next arrow counts from the wrong place. Keep disabled on the item and in rows the same.
  • onSelect(id) is called with the id of the item that was chosen (Enter, Space or a click), and it is called for the Inbox and All items too. A link has already navigated; a button (All) does its work in its own onClick, so put an action in the onClick or in onSelect, not in both.
  • There is no helper to build rows: the ids and labels are the app's own, and a helper would only be the map above. The mistakes are in leaving items out, and the guide and the tests say so.
  • Clicking in the gap between two items of the scrolling middle focuses that region; the arrows then scroll it sideways like any scroller until the next Tab or click puts focus on an item. A click in the gap beside a start or end item focuses nothing.
Prop Values Default Meaning focus useListFocus(...).bar none Makes the bar one keyboard list. Opaque: pass what bar returns, nothing else. Without it the items keep their own Tab stops.

Stories: kit-dock--communities, kit-dock--overflow, kit-dock--phone-bar, kit-dock--communities-light, kit-dock--communities-tinted, kit-dock--focus-twelve, kit-dock--focus-twelve-light, kit-dock--focus-sixty, kit-dock--focus-sixty-phone, kit-dock--fixed-ends, kit-dock--fixed-ends-light, kit-dock--fixed-ends-phone, kit-dock--fixed-ends-tinted.

Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

docs.title: DockItem
docs.text:
One community on the Dock: a round button, or a link, that holds its picture.

Use it when the item is a community in a Dock.

Do not use it when you show a community in a list or a row. Use ListRow with an Avatar. Do not use it outside a Dock.

What the picture shows is also in the name, so a screen reader hears all of it. The name is the community's name, then ", current", then ", 3 unread" or ", new messages", then ", reconnecting", for each that applies. The name also shows in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus; the tooltip only repeats the name, so it is not added to the item's description. A count that is not a finite number shows nothing.

Prop Values Default Meaning name text none (required) The community. It is the accessible name, the tooltip and the source of the initials. src an image address none The picture. colour a colour as #rrggbb none The community's own colour, as for Avatar. current true, false false The community you are in: an accent ring. unread a number 0 A count on the item. 0 shows nothing. unreadLabel unread, mentions unread What the count means, in the name and the badge's label: ", 3 unread", or ", 1 mention" / ", 2 mentions". Use mentions when the number counts mentions. Web kit only so far. newMessages true, false false There are new messages that do not mention you: a small accent dot at the top right, and ", new messages" in the name. With an unread count the badge is shown instead and the dot is not. status reconnecting none A warning dot, and the picture dimmed. onClick a function none Makes the item a button. href an address none Makes the item a link. id text none The id of the element. focus rowFocus(id) from useListFocus none Joins the Dock's keyboard list. See Dock.

The ring is always there and is clear when the item is not current, so becoming current moves nothing. The count is a danger Badge and a warning dot is the dot of a reconnecting community; both are drawn only, and the name carries the same facts. The Dock stories show every state.

The dot says "something new, nobody asked for you" and the count says "someone did": a count wins over the dot. The dot is a shape that is there or not (and the name says it), never a colour change.

Stories: kit-dock--communities, kit-dock--overflow, kit-dock--new-messages, kit-dock--new-messages-light, kit-dock--new-messages-tinted.

Web kit only so far; the native kit has not caught up (see Extending the system).

docs.title: Sheet
docs.text:
A large modal panel for browsing or a longer task, such as a list of all communities or a settings pane.

Use it when the user looks through many things or does a task with several steps, and it needs more room than a question.

Do not use it when the user only answers a question. Use Dialog. Do not use it for a few controls beside the thing they act on. Use Popover.

Use Dialog for a decision and Sheet for browsing or a longer task. A Sheet works like a Dialog: it dims the page and nothing behind it can be used until it closes. The title and a Close button stay at the top. The actions, if any, stay in a row at the bottom. Only the body scrolls. Above the phone width the Sheet is a panel in the middle of the page. On a phone it rises from the bottom as a bottom sheet: full width, rounded at the top, and it leaves room for the Dock. The last row of the bottom sheet (the actions, or the body when there are none) is padded by the home-indicator inset (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) on top of its normal padding. On phones the app shell keeps the sheet above the on-screen keyboard (the viewport setting and the keyboard inset are the shell plan's job, not the kit's).

The parent decides whether the sheet closes. onClose is called on Escape, on a press on the dimmed page and on the Close button, and says which: 'escape', 'scrim' or 'button'. Like a Dialog, a sheet opened from inside another layer closes with it, and onClose is then called with 'parentClosed': a notice, not a request.

Prop Values Default Meaning open true, false none (required) Whether the sheet is showing. onClose a function, given 'escape', 'scrim', 'button' or 'parentClosed' none (required) Called on Escape, on a press on the dimmed page, on Close, and when the layer it was opened from closes. title text none (required) Names the sheet. It is the heading. children content none (required) The body. It scrolls. actions Buttons none The buttons, in a row pinned to the bottom. On a phone they stack. top content none Content fixed under the title, above the scrolling body, such as a heading and a search field that filters the body. It never scrolls out of view. Web kit only so far. size md, lg md The width. md is 560 pixels and lg is 800. opener element what had focus Where focus returns when it closes. For a sheet opened from a layer that closes at the same moment (a "See reactions" row in another sheet), so focus does not return into the gone layer. Web kit only so far.

When there are no actions, focus starts on the Close button (the panel is not a control). With actions, focus lands on the sheet itself, so Close is the first Tab stop. A select list, a Menu, a Popover or a Tooltip may open from inside a Sheet, as in a Dialog.

Stories: kit-sheet--all-communities, kit-sheet--with-actions, kit-sheet--with-top, kit-sheet--long-content, kit-sheet--phone, kit-sheet--all-communities-light, kit-sheet--all-communities-tinted.

docs.title: What the browser does for us
docs.text:
The web kit gets a lot of behaviour for free from the browser and from MUI, and none of it is written down in the components. The native client draws every control itself, so it has to implement each behaviour below on its own. Some of it is now in the shared behaviour tables (see Behaviour), which both clients are tested against. For the rest, this list is the spec for the native side.

When an overlay closes, and where focus goes after, is no longer MUI's to decide. It is the overlay stack's (see Overlay stack): Escape, Tab, a press outside, a closing parent and focus return. The kit turns off MUI's own Escape handling, its focus restore and its close reasons. The lists below say what each overlay still gets from MUI and the browser.

docs.title: Select menu
docs.text:
• The list opens when the pointer is pressed on the field, not when it is released. Enter, Space, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open it from the keyboard.
  • When it opens, focus goes to the selected item, or to the first item when there is none.
  • Typing letters jumps to the next item whose text starts with them. Home and End jump to the first and last item. Disabled items are skipped. The list does not wrap.
  • Tab closes the list and puts focus back on the field; the next Tab moves on. Escape and a click outside close it and put focus back on the field. The list is a menu layer of the overlay stack, which decides all three; MUI only closes it when an option is chosen.
  • While the list is open the page behind it does not scroll, and the page is hidden from assistive technology. Focus cannot leave the list.
  • The list is at least as wide as the field and sits just below it. When there is no room it is moved to stay 16 px inside the window; it does not flip above the field.
  • The list fades in over the fast timing.
  • Clicking the label focuses the field and does not open the list.

docs.title: Text input
docs.text:
• A multiline field grows with its text. It measures the text with a hidden copy of itself.
  • The focus ring shows on any focus, with the mouse too, not only the keyboard.
  • maxLength is enforced by the input itself: typing and pasting stop at the limit.
  • A browser autofill is detected and the field is treated as filled.

docs.title: Slider
docs.text:
• A press on the rail jumps the thumb to that point, and dragging moves it from there. The thumb travels the width of the rail minus its own width, so at both ends it sits fully inside.
  • Values snap to the step grid counted from min. Arrows move one step; Home and End jump to the ends; PageUp and PageDown move a larger step.

docs.title: Radio group
docs.text:
• Tab enters the group at the selected radio, or at the first enabled radio when none is selected (Shift+Tab enters at the last). Only one radio of the group is a Tab stop.
  • Arrows move focus and selection together, skip disabled radios and wrap.

docs.title: Label rows
docs.text: • A press anywhere on the row of a checkbox, switch or radio, the text included, activates the control. A disabled row does nothing.

docs.title: Avatar
docs.text:
• The initials: split the name on whitespace and keep, in each word, only the graphemes that start with a letter, a number or a pictograph. Two or more words give the first grapheme of the first two words; one word gives its first two. Each is upper-cased for the locale, but kept as written if upper-casing would make it longer (ß stays ß). Nothing left gives the User icon, and the accessible name is "Unknown user" for a blank name.
  • The colour search: take the two inks (page and text colours) and call the one with less contrast on black the darker. If the darker ink reads better on the colour, move the colour lighter, otherwise darker, in steps of 0.002 of lightness (Oklch) up to 500 steps. At each step take the better ink and stop at the first that reaches 4.5:1. Keep hue and chroma; chroma drops only where the lightness leaves the colour range. Stop at black or white. A colour that already passes is used as given. If none passes, use the neutral look. Cache the answer per colour and inks.
  • The dot is space.sm across for xs and space.md for the others, and sits border.hairline outside the bottom right corner, with a border.selected ring in the page colour around it. Offline has a border.selected border in the dim text colour around a page-coloured centre. Away has a bar across the middle, border.selected high and the dot's width less two borders wide.
  • The speaking ring is drawn outside the avatar's box: a page-coloured gap border.selected wide, then a ring of the same width in green. It can be clipped by a parent that hides overflow and overlaps its neighbours.
  • A loaded picture hides the initials (they keep their place); a failed one shows them; a new src starts again.

docs.title: Avatar stack
docs.text:
• Each avatar sits in a ring of border.selected in the page colour and overlaps the one before by space.sm.
  • The name: one name is itself, two are "A and B", three or more are "A, B and C", with "and" explicit and not found by looking for a comma in the text. When some are hidden, the shown names are joined by commas and followed by "and N more", or "N people" when none is shown. Blank names read "Unknown user".

docs.title: Badge
docs.text: • The number is floored. Zero, a negative or NaN shows nothing, unless it is a dot. A max below 1 or NaN means 99. Above max it reads "max+".

docs.title: Progress and loading
docs.text:
• LinearProgress clamps the value to 0 to 100, with NaN as 0. The bar is full width and moved left by what is missing, so the right end stays round. The indeterminate bar is 40 percent wide and travels from just off the left edge to just past the right, in a straight line, over four times the slow timing. Under reduced motion it is a full bar at the disabled opacity, still.
  • Skeleton pulses its opacity from 1 to the disabled opacity and back over four times the slow timing, easing in and out, and is still under reduced motion. Text lines are one body line high each, with the bar inset by space.xs above and below.
  • Spinner is a fixed arc turning at a constant rate. Its stroke is 5/44 of its size (5 of the 44 units MUI draws the circle in).

docs.title: Alert and Toast
docs.text:
• The role: danger and warning alerts (a danger toast) are alert; the rest are status. With announce off, all are note.
  • Alert's actions share one row that wraps: with two long labels the second goes to a second line. A single label too long for the row is cut with an ellipsis.
  • Alert's text button is pulled back by the button's side padding, so its label lines up with the text above. The close button is pulled up so its centre meets the first line of text, and right by the space around its icon, so the icon sits on the padding edge.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
• Focus is drawn only for keyboard focus, never after a mouse press.
  • Space activates a button when the key is released; Enter activates it when the key goes down.
  • A busy button stays focusable and ignores both keys and clicks.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
• When it opens, focus goes to the first item that is not disabled. Focus stays inside the menu.
  • ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between items and wrap at the ends. Home and End jump to the first and last item. Typing letters jumps to the next item whose text starts with them; the shortcut keys count as part of an item's text. Disabled items and dividers are skipped.
  • Enter and Space on an item choose it. Choosing calls the item's action, then closes the menu. A disabled item does nothing when clicked.
  • Tab, Escape and a press on the page outside it close it (the overlay stack's rules), and focus goes back to whatever had it before the menu opened, not to the next control. What MUI still gives: the invisible layer that swallows the press, so the control under it is not activated, and preventDefault on the Tab key. A right or middle press outside does not close it.
  • An item that opens a Dialog: the menu closes under the dialog without moving focus, and the dialog returns focus to the menu's button when it closes.
  • Where a click does not focus the button (Safari), focus still returns to the menu's anchor.
  • Typing letters collects into a prefix; the same letter again steps through the matches. Matching is not case sensitive. MUI resets the prefix after about half a second; the shared rule is one second (the typeahead timing, see List focus).
  • While the menu is open the page behind it does not scroll, and the page is hidden from assistive technology.
  • The menu sits just below the anchor, or just above it for the top placements. When there is no room it is moved to stay one gutter inside the window; it does not flip, so a menu near the bottom moves up and can cover its anchor.
  • The menu is at most the window height less a margin tall and scrolls inside. It follows a window resize.
  • It fades in over the fast timing.

docs.title: Popover
docs.text:
• When it opens, focus goes to the first control inside it, or to the panel itself when there is none.
  • Escape closes it, wherever focus is. So does a press anywhere outside the panel and its anchor, and the press carries on to what is under it. A press on the anchor is left to the anchor. Both are the overlay stack's rules; the kit has no code of its own for them.
  • Nothing traps focus, and the page keeps its scroll. Outside a Dialog the panel is placed at the end of the page, so Tab from its last control carries on after the page. Inside a Dialog it is drawn in the Dialog.
  • A press inside a layer that opened from the Popover (a select list, a Menu, a Dialog) is not a press outside it, and Escape closes that layer first. The Escape is ignored while an input method is composing text, and when the focused control uses it.
  • When it closes with focus inside it, or with focus lost, focus goes back to the anchor. When the user moved focus elsewhere (a press on another control), focus stays there.
  • It sits just below or above the anchor. When there is no room it flips to the other side, then shifts along the anchor to stay one gutter inside the window.
  • It follows the anchor when the window or any scrolling box around it scrolls or resizes, but it does not hide when the anchor scrolls out of view. It has no maximum height, so a tall panel can run off the bottom.

docs.title: Tooltip
docs.text:
• A mouse or pen pointer opens it after a short delay. Keyboard focus opens it at once, but only when the focus is keyboard focus, not after a mouse press.
  • A touch never opens it.
  • The control losing focus closes it, and so does moving the pointer away. The tooltip handles both itself.
  • Escape closes it wherever focus is, and goes no further: a dialog under it stays open and the screen does not get the key. It then stays hidden until the pointer or focus leaves the control and comes back. That is the overlay stack's rule.
  • While it is open, the control is linked to it as a description, merged with any description the control has. The control keeps its own name.
  • A tap on a text field, and a touch press on any control, never open it.
  • The panel cannot be hovered. Escape ignores an input method that is composing text, and a focused control still receives the key before the tooltip closes. A press never closes it.
  • It sits on the chosen side of the control. When there is no room it flips to the other side, then shifts to stay one gutter inside the window. It appears with no fade, and it is not in the page while closed.

docs.title: Dialog
docs.text:
• When it opens, focus goes to the first control in the actions row.
  • Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the dialog. Focus cannot leave it.
  • Escape and a press on the dimmed page call onClose. The parent decides whether to close. Both are the overlay stack's rules: MUI's own Escape handling and close reasons are off.
  • When it closes, focus goes back to the element that was focused just before it opened. If that has gone, focus goes to the layer it was in, or to the screen's focus target. This is the stack's rule too: MUI's focus restore is off.
  • A press on the dimmed page closes it only when the press starts and ends there: a drag that starts in the panel and ends on the dimmed page does not. Only the main button counts: a right or middle press does nothing.
  • A layer opened from inside (a select list, a Menu, a Popover, a Tooltip) is drawn within the dialog and takes the key first. The page behind is hidden from assistive technology when the dialog opens, so a layer drawn elsewhere would be hidden too.
  • Long content scrolls inside the panel, which is never taller than the window less the page gutter. Escape is ignored while an input method is composing, and when the focused control uses it.
  • While it is open the page behind it does not scroll, and the page is hidden from assistive technology. The dialog is announced as a dialog, named by its title and described by its description.
  • The dimmed page fades in. The dialog is centred, and keeps the page gutter on each side of a narrow screen. On a phone the action buttons stack, one to a row, safe action on top.
  • Every layer opened from inside is stacked in the order it was opened, and Escape closes the innermost one first. The panel is the surface layer for what it holds, whatever it was opened from (a Card, a selected row).
  • A fade in and out with a duration; reduced motion turns it off.

docs.title: Dock
docs.text:
• A bar that holds more than fits scrolls sideways inside itself. The scrollbar is not drawn, and the scroll does not pass on to the page. While everything fits, the items are centred. Once it overflows they start at the start edge, so nothing is cut off at the left.
  • It keeps the current item (the one marked as the current page) in view when it first shows and whenever the current item changes: it scrolls only as far as needed, leaving the edge fade's width (space.xl) beside the item. A scroll the user made is left alone otherwise. It scrolls the bar, never the page.
  • An item is a button or a link with its own name and a tooltip. The ring of the current item is a border that is always there, so nothing moves when it changes.
  • Scrolling sideways keeps momentum on touch and takes a trackpad's horizontal scroll. Items are centred while they fit and start at the start edge once they overflow (safe center; an old engine that lacks it starts at the start edge, which is acceptable). The bar re-centres the current item when its own size changes.
  • With bottomBar the bar keeps env(safe-area-inset-bottom) as a bottom margin.
  • As a keyboard list (focus) the bar is one Tab stop; the focused item is scrolled into view inside the scrolling region, leaving the fade's width beside it. Firefox makes a scrolling element a Tab stop of its own, so the scrolling region is tabindex="-1".
  • start and end items sit outside the scrolling region. The fade at an edge is a CSS mask that follows the scroll position.
  • A mouse wheel turns vertically: while the middle overflows, a vertical wheel with no sideways part scrolls it sideways, as far as it can go. At the end it is moving to, or when nothing overflows, the wheel goes on to the page. A trackpad's sideways scroll and Ctrl + wheel (zoom) are the browser's.

docs.title: Sheet
docs.text:
• It behaves like a Dialog: the page behind does not scroll and is hidden from assistive technology, focus moves in and cannot leave, Escape and a press on the dimmed page call onClose (the overlay stack decides both), and focus goes back to where it was. A layer opened from inside is drawn within the sheet. Focus goes to the sheet itself.
  • The header and the actions stay put and the body scrolls.
  • Above the phone width it is centred and keeps the page gutter. At the phone width or below it is full width, sits at the bottom with rounded top corners, and is never taller than the window less the height of the Dock. It slides up when it opens, unless the user asks for reduced motion. It fades out when it closes. The actions stack, one to a row.
  • The bottom sheet is a flex column: a fixed header, a body that scrolls with its overscroll kept inside, and the optional fixed actions. Its largest height is relative to the window. The last row clears the home indicator through env(safe-area-inset-bottom). The keyboard inset is not handled here: the app shell keeps the sheet above the on-screen keyboard.
  • With no actions, Close takes focus when it opens.

docs.title: Island and Card
docs.text:
